+[word/document.xml] WORKING DRAFT — VINYL INSTALLATION PROCEDURE INCLUDED: Working draft procedure for vinyl installation using perimeter double-sided tape, hardware relief slits, and mechanical greenhouse snap clamps. Recommended vinyl dimensions (image size, bleed size, overall cut size) and tape strip quantities are provisional and subject to shop fit-up confirmation.

+[word/document.xml] This section governs the preparation, alignment, dual-axis tensioning, relief slit cutting, and mechanical fastening of the custom printed vinyl coverings to completed backdrop upright frames. Installing vinyl on the 10 ft x 8 ft steel frame requires a clean staging area, careful bleed centering, razor relief cuts for protruding frame hardware, double-sided tape adhesion, and mechanical clamping with greenhouse snap clamps to prevent loosening under high stadium wind loads.
+[word/document.xml] Recommended Vinyl Dimensions & Ordering Specifications

+[word/document.xml] Custom printed backdrop banners must be ordered to exact dimensions to provide clean full-bleed framing around the outer perimeter of the steel pipe structure. The specifications below define the required production allowances:
+[word/document.xml] Specification / Parameter
+[word/document.xml] Engineering Requirement / Dimension
+[word/document.xml] Nominal Upright Frame Size
+[word/document.xml] 8 ft Width × 10 ft Height (96.0 in. × 120.0 in. outer pipe perimeter)
+[word/document.xml] Visible Graphic / Live Face
+[word/document.xml] [TBD] in. Width × [TBD] in. Height (Front visible image area)
+[word/document.xml] Perimeter Bleed Wrap Allowance
+[word/document.xml] [TBD] in. per border (top, bottom, left, and right outer pipe wrap)
+[word/document.xml] Overall Flat Cut Size
+[word/document.xml] [TBD] in. Width × [TBD] in. Height (Including bleed allowance)
+[word/document.xml] Substrate Material
+[word/document.xml] 13 oz or 18 oz heavy-duty outdoor matte scrim vinyl (UV and tear resistant)
+[word/document.xml] Edge Perimeter Finish
+[word/document.xml] Square raw-cut perimeter; DO NOT order hemmed borders or brass grommets, as raw edges wrap smoothly under snap clamps.
+[word/document.xml] Required Materials & Fastening Hardware

+[word/document.xml] • Moving blankets: Three to four clean, heavy-duty moving blankets or carpet runners spread across the shop floor to cushion the printed vinyl face against dust, grit, and concrete abrasion.

+[word/document.xml] • Custom vinyl banner: One custom printed outdoor banner per backdrop (nominal 8 ft x 10 ft), rolled with print side facing inward. Unroll and inspect for print flaws and correct orientation prior to assembly.
+[word/document.xml] • Utility knife / razor: Fresh, sharp razor knife for cutting precision relief slits around mounting brackets and tension bands.

+[word/document.xml] • Double-sided tape: 1-in. wide heavy-duty outdoor mounting tape (Appendix B Table 1). Cut into fourteen (14) strips of approximately 4-in. length (~56 linear inches per frame). Application schedule: 4 strips on each vertical upright rail (8 total) and 3 strips on each cross rail (6 total). Tape quantities are provisional (TBD) and will be validated during build testing.

+[word/document.xml] • Greenhouse snap clamps: Fourteen (14) 1-1/4 in. greenhouse clamp clips (Appendix B Index [8]). Snapped directly over the wrapped vinyl at every tape location (4 along each long vertical rail, 3 along each short cross rail). Note: While the frame uses 1-5/8 in. outer diameter fence post tubing, 1-1/4 in. greenhouse clamp clips provide the proper snug snap fit over the tubing, vinyl, and tape.

+[word/document.xml] • Surface preparation (Optional): Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and clean microfiber cloth. Degreasing the steel pipe is completely optional—the heavy-duty tape combined with mechanical greenhouse snap clamps provides more than enough holding power. A weaker initial adhesive bond to the bare steel pipe is actually preferable, as it significantly simplifies tape removal and cleanup later.
+[word/document.xml] • Personnel requirement: Minimum two operators required; three to four recommended for synchronized dual-operator transverse tensioning and safe frame lifting.
+[word/document.xml] Step-by-Step Vinyl Installation Procedure
+[word/document.xml] Step 1: Staging and Surface Protection

+[word/document.xml] Clear an unobstructed shop workspace measuring at least 12 ft x 14 ft. Thoroughly sweep and vacuum the area to remove metal chips, drill burrs, or grit that could puncture or scratch the printed vinyl face.
+[word/document.xml] Lay clean moving blankets flat across the floor, overlapping edges to create a continuous, cushioned staging area larger than the overall banner flat cut size.

+[word/document.xml] Carefully unroll the custom vinyl banner and lay it completely face down directly onto the moving blankets. Smooth the banner flat by hand and inspect the back side to confirm it is clean and free of trapped debris.
+[word/document.xml] Step 2: Frame Placement and Bleed Alignment

+[word/document.xml] With two operators lifting opposite ends, carry the assembled 10 ft x 8 ft steel upright frame onto the staging area and place it face down centered over the back side of the vinyl banner.

+[word/document.xml] Measure the bleed wrap margin extending beyond the outer edge of the steel tubing along all four perimeter borders. Shift the frame incrementally until an equal reveal of bleed extends evenly on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right outer rails).
+[word/document.xml] Verify frame squareness by measuring crossed diagonals prior to applying tape or making relief cuts.
+[word/document.xml] Step 3: Hardware Relief Slits

+[word/document.xml] Before adhering tape or wrapping vinyl, use a fresh, sharp utility razor knife to make small, neat relief slits in the vinyl bleed wrap allowance to accommodate protruding frame hardware:

+[word/document.xml] • Long edges (Vertical Uprights): Cut small slits directly aligned with the diagonal support strut attachment brackets (tension bands) on the left and right upright rails. These slits allow the strut brackets to protrude through the bleed wrap cleanly, preventing unsightly puckering, tenting, or bunching of the visible banner face.

+[word/document.xml] • Bottom edge (Cart-Mounting Interface): Cut two small relief slits along the bottom rail bleed wrap corresponding to the base tension bands and mounting brackets that secure the upright frame to the wood cart base.
+[word/document.xml] Step 4: Perimeter Double-Sided Tape Application
+[word/document.xml] Cut fourteen (14) strips of 1-in. heavy-duty double-sided tape, each approximately 4 inches in length.
+[word/document.xml] Apply the tape strips to the rear-facing surface of the perimeter steel fence post tubing according to the following layout:

+[word/document.xml] • Long rails (Left and Right 10-ft Vertical Uprights): Apply 4 strips along each upright (8 total). Crucially, position two of the strips immediately above and below the support strut bracket to anchor the vinyl around the bracket interface, and place two additional strips spaced along the remaining length of each upright.

+[word/document.xml] • Short end rails (Top and Bottom 8-ft Cross Rails): Apply 3 strips evenly spaced along each rail (one centered and two approximately 6 inches inward from the corner brackets; 6 strips total).
+[word/document.xml] Burnish each tape strip firmly onto the steel pipe surface, then peel and discard the protective release liners from all 14 strips.
+[word/document.xml] Step 5: Long-Side Tensioning and Initial Wrap

+[word/document.xml] Start along one designated long side (left vertical upright). Beginning at the support strut bracket, ease the bracket through its pre-cut relief slit, fold the vinyl bleed margin tightly around the steel pipe, and press it firmly into the 4 double-sided tape strips on the rear of the tube.

+[word/document.xml] Move to the opposing long side (right vertical upright). Pull the vinyl firmly across the frame face to eliminate all slack and wrinkles. Ease the second support strut bracket through its relief slit, fold the vinyl edge tightly around the steel pipe, and press it securely into the 4 opposing tape strips.
+[word/document.xml] Sight down the front face: confirm that longitudinal tension is smooth, uniform, and drum-tight, with no diagonal wrinkling or wave patterns.
+[word/document.xml] Step 6: Short-Side Dual-Operator Tensioning and Wrap
+[word/document.xml] Station operators at opposite short ends (top cross rail and bottom cross rail).

+[word/document.xml] Working simultaneously, both operators firmly grasp the vinyl bleed margin on opposite ends and pull outward in opposing directions away from the center. This synchronized outward pull establishes balanced transverse tension across the entire frame without racking the structure out of square.

+[word/document.xml] While maintaining continuous outward tension, wrap the top vinyl edge over the top cross rail and press into the 3 tape strips. At the bottom rail, guide the cart-mounting base brackets through their two pre-cut relief slits, wrap the vinyl edge tightly around the bottom pipe, and press into the 3 bottom tape strips.
+[word/document.xml] Neatly fold excess vinyl corner tabs around the 3-way corner elbow brackets, flattening the material to maintain clean, square corners without bulky bunches.
+[word/document.xml] Step 7: Greenhouse Snap Clamp Installation

+[word/document.xml] Install the 1-1/4 in. greenhouse snap clamps directly over the wrapped vinyl at every tape location, pressing each clamp firmly over the pipe until it snaps into full mechanical lock:

+[word/document.xml] • Long rails (Vertical Uprights): Install 4 snap clamps on each upright (8 clamps total). Crucially, position two of the snap clamps immediately above and below each support strut bracket to firmly sandwich and hold the bracket in place, preventing bracket slip, flutter, or vinyl detachment under wind loads.
+[word/document.xml] • Short end rails (Top and Bottom Cross Rails): Install 3 snap clamps on the top rail and 3 snap clamps on the bottom rail (6 clamps total).

+[word/document.xml] The 1-1/4 in. greenhouse snap clamps compress the vinyl tightly against the tape and 1-5/8 in. steel fence post tubing, providing heavy-duty mechanical clamping that prevents edge detachment under stadium wind gusts or rough transport handling.
+[word/document.xml] Confirm that no snap clamp interferes with the cart-mounting base brackets or corner elbow clamp bolts.
+[word/document.xml] Step 8: Final Tension Inspection and Frame Re-Mounting
+[word/document.xml] With three to four operators, carefully lift the completed backdrop frame upright off the moving blankets.

+[word/document.xml] Inspect the front vinyl face in bright lighting: verify that the graphic is drum-tight, square, free of wrinkles or sagging, and cleanly fitted around all protruding bracket slits.
+[word/document.xml] Verify that all 14 greenhouse snap clamps are fully seated and firmly gripping the tubing over each tape strip.

+[word/document.xml] Re-secure the vertical upright posts into the cart base tension bands and re-connect the diagonal support struts. Confirm that the wrapped vinyl and snap clamps do not bind or impede strut attachment.
[word/document.xml] Figure 6. Installation team applying carpet tape and securing vinyl banner with pipe snap clamps.
+[word/document.xml] Vinyl Removal & End-of-Season Teardown Protocol

+[word/document.xml] CAUTION — Temperature Requirement for Vinyl Removal: Do not attempt removal of the vinyl or adhesive tape unless the ambient temperature is above 80°F (27°C). Attempting to peel the vinyl at lower temperatures will cause the material to tear and permanently damage the custom banner face. In cooler weather, warm the shop or gently heat the taped perimeter with a heat gun on low before peeling.
+[word/document.xml] When taking down backdrops or preparing frames for graphic replacement:

+[word/document.xml] • Recommended timing (Defer to Band Camp): It is usually much easier to leave the vinyl on the frames over the winter and wait until summer band camp of the following season before attempting removal. Cold late-fall temperatures following competition season make adhesive stiff and brittle, drastically increasing tear risk.

+[word/document.xml] • Solar heating advantage: The warmer it is outside, the better. Staging the backdrops outdoors in direct sunlight for just a few minutes prior to peeling warms the steel tubing and softens the tape adhesive, allowing the vinyl and tape to release cleanly and effortlessly with minimal pull resistance.
+[word/document.xml] • Remove greenhouse snap clamps: Carefully pry off all 14 greenhouse snap clamps from the perimeter tubing.

+[word/document.xml] • Peel slowly at shallow angle: Starting at one corner, slowly peel the vinyl wrap back at a shallow angle. Warm adhesive releases cleanly from the bare steel pipe without pulling the scrim or ink layer.

+[word/document.xml] • Tape stripping & cleanup: Peel remaining tape strips from the steel pipe. Because the pipe was not aggressively degreased during initial assembly, tape strips will pull off cleanly with minimal adhesive residue.

[word/document.xml] □ Cart Base Squareness: Opposite diagonal measurements within 1/8 in.
